notes: Verifier passes 27/27 on the AOT binary at workdir/taskman (source: taskman.misa). Key design decisions: exit code 1 via print('Error: ...') + uncaught throw (AOT exits 1 with a one-line 'line:col: CODE: msg' report on stderr — no traceback); env-var defaults via try/catch around env() (E302); id validation by manual digit scan (str.ord/str.slice) rather than int() to reject '0', '-3', ' 5', 'abc'; SQL injection avoided by binding titles with '?' placeholders while interpolating only validated-int ids and fixed status literals; import validates array-ness by checking the trimmed text starts with '[' then json.parse in try/catch (parse errors can't be distinguished from field-access errors otherwise); bad-status import items produce 'Error: bad status'. Edge cases verified manually beyond the verifier: bad ids, 23-digit ids (no task #<raw>), injection title stored literally, non-array JSON, empty array import, unknown command prints error + usage with exit 1. Hardest parts were Misa-specific: the '{{'/'}}' interpolation trap and the missing else-if. Typed 'table tasks' + db.query gave compile-time column checking for free.
